pages.heading: System of linear equations and matrix form

blocks.text: System is consistent (at least one sol) if \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)\) — augmented.
Set of linear equations in 2 or more unknowns is called system of linear equations.
The above system can be written in matrix form as \(AX=B\), where A is the coefficient matrix, X is the column of unknowns and B is the column of constants.
A system is said to be consistent if it has at least 1 sol.
Consider the above system \(AX=B\). This system is said to be consistent if and only if \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)\).
Case (ii): \(\rho(A)=\rho(A|B)<n\) ⇒ infinite solutions; \((n-r)\) may be taken as independent parameters when the common rank is r.
If \(\rho(A)\ne\rho(A|B)\) ⇒ system has no solution and is inconsistent.
System \(AX=B\) is said to be non-homogeneous if \(B\ne0\).
A non-homogeneous system may or may not be consistent.
System of form \(AX=0\) is called homogeneous where 0 is null vector.
A homogeneous system is always consistent as it possesses a trivial solution.
A homogeneous system with \(AX=0\) will have a non-trivial solution iff \(\rho(A)<n\); for a square coefficient matrix, equivalently \(|A|=0\).
